blocks.en: "Hear, O Israel: The LORD our God, the LORD is one!" — Deuteronomy 6:4 (NKJV)
blocks.es_reference: "Oye, Israel: Jehová nuestro Dios, Jehová uno es." — Deuteronomio 6:4 (RVG)

blocks.en: God Is — The Question Behind Every Question
blocks.es_reference: Dios Es — La Pregunta Detrás de Cada Pregunta

blocks.en: Open any Bible, anywhere, and watch what God refuses to do. He does not argue for His existence. He does not file a logical proof in chapter one. He simply begins: "In the beginning God created" (Genesis 1:1). Theology proper — the doctrine of God — starts where Scripture starts. Not with a court case but with a confession. The God of the Bible is, has always been, and never will not be. The question is not whether you believe in Him; the question is what you do once you discover He believes you exist.
blocks.es_reference: Abra cualquier Biblia, en cualquier lugar, y observe lo que Dios se niega a hacer. No argumenta a favor de Su existencia. No presenta una prueba lógica en el capítulo uno. Simplemente comienza: "En el principio creó Dios" (Génesis 1:1). La teología propia — la doctrina de Dios — comienza donde comienza la Escritura. No con un proceso judicial sino con una confesión. El Dios de la Biblia es, siempre ha sido, y nunca dejará de ser. La pregunta no es si usted cree en Él; la pregunta es qué hace usted una vez que descubre que Él cree que usted existe.

blocks.en: When Moses asks God for a name to carry back to Egypt, the answer is shocking. "I AM WHO I AM" (Exodus 3:14). That is not a name in the way Pharaoh would understand a name. It is a refusal to be defined by anything outside Himself. Every other being in the universe is contingent — leaves depend on trees, trees depend on soil, soil depends on a planet, the planet depends on a star. Trace the chain back and you discover that everything that exists is borrowed. Everything except One. He is the great Uncaused Cause, the necessary being on whom all other being depends. Theologians call this aseity — God's life from Himself. It is the foundation of every other thing we will say about Him.
blocks.es_reference: Cuando Moisés le pide a Dios un nombre para llevarlo de vuelta a Egipto, la respuesta es asombrosa. "YO SOY EL QUE SOY" (Éxodo 3:14). Eso no es un nombre como Faraón entendería un nombre. Es un rechazo a ser definido por algo fuera de Sí mismo. Cada otro ser en el universo es contingente — las hojas dependen de los árboles, los árboles dependen del suelo, el suelo depende de un planeta, el planeta depende de una estrella. Rastree la cadena hacia atrás y descubrirá que todo lo que existe es prestado. Todo excepto Uno. Él es la gran Causa No Causada, el ser necesario del cual depende todo otro ser. Los teólogos llaman a esto aseidad — la vida de Dios desde Sí mismo. Es el fundamento de cada otra cosa que diremos acerca de Él.

blocks.en: And here is the twist. The same God who needs nothing from you wants you anyway. Aseity is not a cold doctrine. It is the reason the cross is grace. God did not save you because He was lonely. He saved you because He chose to.
blocks.es_reference: Y aquí está el giro. El mismo Dios que no necesita nada de usted lo quiere a usted de todos modos. La aseidad no es una doctrina fría. Es la razón por la que la cruz es gracia. Dios no lo salvó porque estuviera solo. Lo salvó porque Él eligió hacerlo.

blocks.en: The Incommunicable Attributes
blocks.es_reference: Los Atributos Incomunicables

blocks.en: Some of God's qualities are His alone. He does not share them; He cannot share them; the moment you tried to imitate them, you would be claiming to be God. We call these the incommunicable attributes.
blocks.es_reference: Algunas de las cualidades de Dios son sólo Suyas. Él no las comparte; no puede compartirlas; en el momento en que usted intentara imitarlas, estaría reclamando ser Dios. Llamamos a estos los atributos incomunicables.

blocks.en: He is eternal — without beginning, without end. "From everlasting to everlasting You are God" (Psalm 90:2). Your story begins at a hospital. His does not begin.
blocks.es_reference: Él es eterno — sin principio, sin fin. "Desde el siglo y hasta el siglo, Tú eres Dios" (Salmo 90:2). Su historia comienza en un hospital. La de Él no comienza.

blocks.en: He is immutable — He does not change. Not in essence, not in character, not in promises. "I am the LORD, I do not change" (Malachi 3:6). The God who comforted Hannah in 1 Samuel is the same God who comforts you tonight, and not by an inch is He different.
blocks.es_reference: Él es inmutable — Él no cambia. Ni en esencia, ni en carácter, ni en promesas. "Porque yo Jehová no cambio" (Malaquías 3:6). El Dios que consoló a Ana en 1 Samuel es el mismo Dios que lo consuela a usted esta noche, y ni por un milímetro es diferente.

blocks.en: He is omnipresent — wholly present everywhere. David asks the question and despairs of finding an escape: "Where can I go from Your Spirit?" (Psalm 139:7). The honest answer is: nowhere. The hospital room, the prison cell, the empty house, the airplane at 35,000 feet — He is fully there.
blocks.es_reference: Él es omnipresente — totalmente presente en todas partes. David hace la pregunta y se desespera de encontrar un escape: "¿A dónde me iré de tu Espíritu?" (Salmo 139:7). La respuesta honesta es: a ninguna parte. La habitación del hospital, la celda de la prisión, la casa vacía, el avión a 35,000 pies — Él está plenamente allí.

blocks.en: More Incommunicable Attributes
blocks.es_reference: Más Atributos Incomunicables

blocks.en: He is omniscient — knowing all things, actual and possible, past, present, and future. He does not learn. He does not guess. "All things are naked and open to the eyes of Him to whom we must give account" (Hebrews 4:13). You have never had a thought God did not anticipate.
blocks.es_reference: Él es omnisciente — conoce todas las cosas, actuales y posibles, pasadas, presentes y futuras. Él no aprende. No adivina. "Todas las cosas están desnudas y abiertas a los ojos de aquel a quien tenemos que dar cuenta" (Hebreos 4:13). Usted nunca ha tenido un pensamiento que Dios no anticipara.

blocks.en: He is omnipotent — He can do all things consistent with His nature. He cannot lie because He is truth; that is not a limitation but a perfection. He spoke galaxies into being and is more than able to handle the situation that has you awake at three in the morning.
blocks.es_reference: Él es omnipotente — puede hacer todas las cosas consistentes con Su naturaleza. No puede mentir porque Él es la verdad; eso no es una limitación sino una perfección. Él habló galaxias a la existencia y es más que capaz de manejar la situación que lo tiene despierto a las tres de la mañana.

blocks.en: He is sovereign. Daniel learned it the hard way watching Babylon rise and fall: "He does according to His will in the army of heaven and among the inhabitants of the earth" (Daniel 4:35). Sovereignty is not God shoving people around; it is God ruling, ordering, and overruling so that His purpose stands.
blocks.es_reference: Él es soberano. Daniel lo aprendió de la manera difícil viendo a Babilonia ascender y caer: "Hace según su voluntad en el ejército del cielo, y en los habitantes de la tierra" (Daniel 4:35). La soberanía no es Dios empujando a la gente; es Dios gobernando, ordenando y sobre-gobernando para que Su propósito permanezca.

blocks.en: The Communicable Attributes
blocks.es_reference: Los Atributos Comunicables

blocks.en: Other qualities of God are shared in measure with His image-bearers. We will never be infinite, but we can be truthful. We will never be omnipotent, but we can be holy. These are the communicable attributes.
blocks.es_reference: Otras cualidades de Dios son compartidas en medida con Sus portadores de imagen. Nunca seremos infinitos, pero podemos ser veraces. Nunca seremos omnipotentes, pero podemos ser santos. Estos son los atributos comunicables.

blocks.en: He is holy — set apart, pure, morally perfect. Isaiah hears it in the throne room: "Holy, Holy, Holy is the LORD of hosts" (Isaiah 6:3). Triple holiness. The Hebrew language has no superlative form, so when something needs to be elevated to the maximum degree, the word is repeated. "Holy, holy" would be the most holy. "Holy, holy, holy" is the language of an angel running out of vocabulary.
blocks.es_reference: Él es santo — apartado, puro, moralmente perfecto. Isaías lo escucha en la sala del trono: "Santo, santo, santo, Jehová de los ejércitos" (Isaías 6:3). Triple santidad. El idioma hebreo no tiene una forma superlativa, así que cuando algo necesita ser elevado al grado máximo, la palabra se repite. "Santo, santo" sería lo más santo. "Santo, santo, santo" es el lenguaje de un ángel quedándose sin vocabulario.

blocks.en: He is righteous — always doing what is right, by His own perfect standard. He is just — rendering to every party exactly what is due. "Shall not the Judge of all the earth do right?" (Genesis 18:25).
blocks.es_reference: Él es recto — siempre hace lo correcto, según Su propio estándar perfecto. Él es justo — entregando a cada parte exactamente lo que se debe. "¿No ha de hacer justicia el Juez de toda la tierra?" (Génesis 18:25).

blocks.en: He is love. "He who does not love does not know God, for God is love" (1 John 4:8). The text does not say God has love or shows love. God is love. Before there was a creation to love, the Father loved the Son, the Son loved the Father, and the Spirit was the love between them. Love did not begin at the manger. The manger is what love does.
blocks.es_reference: Él es amor. "El que no ama no ha conocido a Dios; porque Dios es amor" (1 Juan 4:8). El texto no dice que Dios tiene amor o muestra amor. Dios es amor. Antes de que hubiera una creación que amar, el Padre amaba al Hijo, el Hijo amaba al Padre, y el Espíritu era el amor entre ellos. El amor no comenzó en el pesebre. El pesebre es lo que el amor hace.

blocks.en: He is merciful — slow to anger and ready to forgive. He is gracious — giving good gifts to those who have not earned them. The single thing keeping you out of hell tonight is grace, and grace is not a thing. Grace is who God is. He is faithful. He keeps His word. Across the longest pause in your prayer life, He is still keeping it.
blocks.es_reference: Él es misericordioso — tardo para la ira y listo para perdonar. Él es de gracia — dando buenos dones a aquellos que no los han ganado. La única cosa que lo mantiene a usted fuera del infierno esta noche es la gracia, y la gracia no es una cosa. La gracia es quien Dios es. Él es fiel. Cumple Su palabra. A través de la pausa más larga en su vida de oración, Él todavía la está cumpliendo.

blocks.en: One God in Three Persons
blocks.es_reference: Un Dios en Tres Personas

blocks.en: Now we turn the corner into the most stretching doctrine in the Bible. The Shema of Israel is unambiguous: "Hear, O Israel: The LORD our God, the LORD is one!" (Deuteronomy 6:4). One God. Not three gods. Not one God with three masks. One God.
blocks.es_reference: Ahora doblamos la esquina hacia la doctrina más estirante en la Biblia. El Shemá de Israel es inequívoco: "Oye, Israel: Jehová nuestro Dios, Jehová uno es" (Deuteronomio 6:4). Un Dios. No tres dioses. No un Dios con tres máscaras. Un Dios.

blocks.en: And yet — when Jesus is baptized, the Son stands in the water, the Spirit descends like a dove, and the Father speaks from heaven (Matthew 3:16-17). Three persons, simultaneously, in three distinct actions. At the Great Commission Jesus baptizes "in the name" — singular — "of the Father and of the Son and of the Holy Spirit" (Matthew 28:19). One name, three persons.
blocks.es_reference: Y sin embargo — cuando Jesús es bautizado, el Hijo está de pie en el agua, el Espíritu desciende como paloma, y el Padre habla desde el cielo (Mateo 3:16-17). Tres personas, simultáneamente, en tres acciones distintas. En la Gran Comisión Jesús bautiza "en el nombre" — singular — "del Padre, y del Hijo, y del Espíritu Santo" (Mateo 28:19). Un nombre, tres personas.

blocks.en: The Trinity is the answer. One God, three persons, one in essence, distinct in person. The Father is not the Son. The Son is not the Spirit. The Spirit is not the Father. And yet each is fully God, not one-third God. This is not a contradiction; it is a mystery, and the difference matters. A contradiction violates logic. A mystery exceeds it.
blocks.es_reference: La Trinidad es la respuesta. Un Dios, tres personas, uno en esencia, distintos en persona. El Padre no es el Hijo. El Hijo no es el Espíritu. El Espíritu no es el Padre. Y sin embargo cada uno es plenamente Dios, no un tercio de Dios. Esto no es una contradicción; es un misterio, y la diferencia importa. Una contradicción viola la lógica. Un misterio la excede.

blocks.en: Why does this matter for you on a Tuesday afternoon? Because every relationship you long for has its origin in the Trinity. God did not create because He was bored or short on company. The persons of the Godhead loved one another perfectly before time began. When He saves you, He is not granting you a contract; He is bringing you into a family that has been celebrating long before you arrived.
blocks.es_reference: ¿Por qué importa esto para usted un martes por la tarde? Porque cada relación que usted anhela tiene su origen en la Trinidad. Dios no creó porque estuviera aburrido o le faltara compañía. Las personas de la Deidad se amaban perfectamente antes de que el tiempo comenzara. Cuando Él lo salva, no le está concediendo un contrato; lo está trayendo a una familia que ha estado celebrando mucho antes de que usted llegara.

blocks.en: The God Who Decrees and Rules
blocks.es_reference: El Dios que Decreta y Gobierna

blocks.en: God's decree is His eternal plan — comprehensive, wise, free, and certain. Ephesians 1:11 says He "works all things according to the counsel of His will." All things. Not most things. Not the easy things.
blocks.es_reference: El decreto de Dios es Su plan eterno — comprensivo, sabio, libre y cierto. Efesios 1:11 dice que Él "hace todas las cosas según el designio de su voluntad." Todas las cosas. No la mayoría de las cosas. No las cosas fáciles.

blocks.en: Hold that next to human responsibility. Acts 2:23 says Jesus was delivered up "by the determined purpose and foreknowledge of God" and that "lawless hands" crucified Him. One sentence. Both truths. God ordained the cross. Men freely committed the cross. Both are true. Both are taught. Neither is canceled by the other.
blocks.es_reference: Sostenga eso junto a la responsabilidad humana. Hechos 2:23 dice que Jesús fue entregado "por el determinado consejo y anticipado conocimiento de Dios" y que "manos inicuas" lo crucificaron. Una oración. Ambas verdades. Dios ordenó la cruz. Los hombres libremente cometieron la cruz. Ambas son verdaderas. Ambas son enseñadas. Ninguna es cancelada por la otra.

blocks.en: This is the God you serve. He is not surprised. He is not anxious. The economy is not too big for Him; your medical diagnosis is not too small for Him. The doctrine of providence is not abstract philosophy — it is the hand that holds the worst news you ever received and refuses to let it have the last word.
blocks.es_reference: Este es el Dios al que usted sirve. Él no se sorprende. No está ansioso. La economía no es demasiado grande para Él; su diagnóstico médico no es demasiado pequeño para Él. La doctrina de la providencia no es filosofía abstracta — es la mano que sostiene las peores noticias que usted jamás recibió y se niega a dejar que tengan la última palabra.

blocks.en: So What?
blocks.es_reference: ¿Entonces qué?

blocks.en: If God is who Scripture says He is, three responses follow.
blocks.es_reference: Si Dios es quien la Escritura dice que es, tres respuestas se siguen.

blocks.en: First, worship. You were made for it. Anything less than this God will eventually disappoint you. Worship is not the icing on a Christian life; it is the whole cake. Reverence, awe, song, silence, obedience — all of it is the right response to the God who is.
blocks.es_reference: Primero, adoración. Usted fue hecho para ella. Cualquier cosa menos que este Dios eventualmente lo decepcionará. La adoración no es el glaseado sobre una vida cristiana; es el pastel entero. Reverencia, asombro, canto, silencio, obediencia — todo es la respuesta correcta al Dios que es.

blocks.en: Trust and Proclamation
blocks.es_reference: Confianza y Proclamación

blocks.en: Second, trust. Aseity, sovereignty, faithfulness, omniscience — those are not abstract terms. They are the reason you can sleep tonight. The same God who runs the galaxies is paying attention to your bank account, your blood test, and your child who has not called in three weeks.
blocks.es_reference: Segundo, confianza. Aseidad, soberanía, fidelidad, omnisciencia — esos no son términos abstractos. Son la razón por la que usted puede dormir esta noche. El mismo Dios que dirige las galaxias está prestando atención a su cuenta bancaria, su análisis de sangre, y su hijo que no ha llamado en tres semanas.

blocks.en: Third, proclamation. People are not running from a small God; they are running from the only God there is. Your job is not to invent Him for them. Your job is to introduce them. When you tell people who God is, you are not selling a product — you are reporting an existing reality. He was here before the conversation began. He will be here long after.
blocks.es_reference: Tercero, proclamación. La gente no está huyendo de un Dios pequeño; están huyendo del único Dios que hay. Su trabajo no es inventarlo para ellos. Su trabajo es presentarlo. Cuando usted le dice a la gente quién es Dios, no está vendiendo un producto — está reportando una realidad existente. Él estaba aquí antes de que la conversación comenzara. Estará aquí mucho después.

mc.why: Aseity is the doctrine that God exists from Himself, the necessary being on whom all other being depends.

mc.stem: When God told Moses His name was "I AM WHO I AM" (Exodus 3:14), He was revealing primarily:
mc.why: The "I AM" name discloses God's self-existence — He is, depending on nothing.

mc.why: Psalm 90:2 highlights God's eternity — no beginning, no end.

mc.why: Immutability means God does not change. Malachi 3:6 says it directly.

mc.why: David's question highlights God's omnipresence — He is wholly present everywhere.

mc.stem: The triple cry "Holy, Holy, Holy" in Isaiah 6 functions in Hebrew as:
options: A reference to the Trinity only
mc.why: Hebrew has no superlative form, so repetition is the highest possible degree — triple holiness is maximum holiness.

mc.stem: "God is love" (1 John 4:8) means most precisely:
options: Love is part of God's essential being
Love is God's most important act
mc.why: The text says God is love — love is part of His essential being, not merely something He does.

mc.stem: The Shema (Deuteronomy 6:4) declares:
options: The LORD our God, the LORD is one
mc.why: The Shema is Israel's foundational confession: the LORD our God, the LORD is one.

mc.stem: The Trinity teaches that God is:
options: One God appearing in three modes
mc.why: The Trinity confesses one God in three persons — one in essence, distinct in person.

mc.stem: At Jesus' baptism, the three persons of the Trinity are revealed by:
options: The Son in the water, the Spirit as a dove, the Father speaking
The Father standing in the water
The Spirit speaking, the Son descending
mc.why: Matthew 3:16-17 shows three persons in three distinct simultaneous actions — Son in water, Spirit descending, Father speaking.

mc.stem: The Great Commission's baptismal formula in Matthew 28:19 uses:
options: Only the name of the Father
mc.why: Matthew 28:19 says "in the name" — singular — of the Father, the Son, and the Holy Spirit. One name, three persons.

mc.stem: The eternal plan by which God governs all things is called:
mc.why: God's decree is His eternal plan — comprehensive, wise, free, and certain (Ephesians 1:11).

mc.stem: Acts 2:23 says Jesus was delivered up by God's determined purpose AND killed by "lawless hands." This teaches:
options: God did not really plan the cross
Divine sovereignty and human responsibility are both true
Only one side of the cross is real
mc.why: Acts 2:23 holds both sides together: God ordained the cross; lawless hands committed it. Both are true.

mc.stem: "Incommunicable attributes" are attributes:
mc.why: Incommunicable attributes — like aseity, eternity, immutability — belong to God alone and cannot be shared with creatures.

mc.stem: Which attribute is communicable (shared in measure with image-bearers)?
mc.why: Holiness is a communicable attribute — God commands "Be holy, for I am holy" (1 Peter 1:16). Aseity, immutability, and eternity belong to God alone.

mc.stem: "He works all things according to the counsel of His will" (Ephesians 1:11) most directly teaches:
mc.why: Ephesians 1:11 is a flagship text for God's sovereignty — He works all things according to His will.

mc.stem: Omniscience means God knows:
options: All things actual and possible, past, present, and future
mc.why: Omniscience is exhaustive — past, present, future, actual and possible. God never learns or guesses.

mc.stem: Omnipotence is best defined as:
options: God can do absolutely anything, including contradictions
God can do all things consistent with His nature
God can do whatever humans request
mc.why: Omnipotence is the power to do all things consistent with God's own nature. He cannot lie because He is truth — that is perfection, not limitation.

mc.stem: The distinction between a contradiction and a mystery in the Trinity is:
options: A contradiction violates logic; a mystery exceeds it
mc.why: A contradiction breaks logic; a mystery surpasses logic. The Trinity is not 1=3; it is one in essence, three in person. Mystery, not contradiction.

mc.stem: The proper first response to the doctrine of God is:
mc.why: The doctrine of God is not first an object of study but a call to worship. You were made for it.

sa.prompt: Define the term "aseity" in your own words, and explain why it is called the foundation of every other attribute.
sa.model: Aseity means that God's life is from Himself: He exists on His own and depends on nothing outside Himself. Every other being in the universe is contingent, borrowing its existence from something else, the way leaves depend on a tree and the tree depends on the soil. Trace that chain back far enough and you reach the one being who is not borrowed at all, the great Uncaused Cause, the necessary being on whom all other being depends. It is called the foundation of every other attribute because everything else we say about God rests on the fact that He simply is, needing nothing. And the comfort hidden in it is that the God who needs nothing from you still chose to save you.

sa.prompt: According to Exodus 3:14, what name did God reveal to Moses, and what does it signify?
sa.model: When Moses asked God for a name to carry back to Egypt, God answered, "I AM WHO I AM" (Exodus 3:14). This is not a name in the ordinary way Pharaoh would understand one; it is God's refusal to be defined by anything outside Himself. The name discloses His self-existence, that He simply is, depending on nothing and answerable to no one above Him. While every creature is contingent and borrowed, God names Himself as the One who always was and always will be. So the name is really a confession of His aseity and eternity wrapped into one stunning reply.

sa.prompt: What is the difference between communicable and incommunicable attributes? Give an example of each.
sa.model: Incommunicable attributes are the qualities God alone possesses and cannot share; the moment a creature tried to claim them, it would be claiming to be God. Examples include aseity, eternity, immutability, omnipresence, omniscience, and omnipotence, all of which belong to God by nature. Communicable attributes are qualities God shares in measure with His image-bearers. We will never be infinite or all-powerful, but we can be truthful, and we can be holy, because God commands us to reflect Him. So the line between the two is whether the attribute can be reflected in a creature at all: holiness and love can be, but self-existence and eternity cannot.

sa.prompt: State one incommunicable attribute of God and briefly explain what it means.
sa.model: One incommunicable attribute of God is immutability, which means that God does not change in essence, in character, or in His promises. Malachi 3:6 states it directly: "I am the LORD, I do not change." The God who comforted Hannah long ago is the same God who comforts a believer tonight, not different by even an inch. This sets Him apart from every creature, whose moods, strength, and circumstances shift constantly. Because He does not change, His promises are as reliable on your worst day as on your best, and that steadiness is something no creature could ever possess in itself.

sa.prompt: State one communicable attribute of God and briefly explain what it means.
sa.model: One communicable attribute of God is holiness, which means He is set apart, pure, and morally perfect. Isaiah heard it cried in the throne room, "Holy, Holy, Holy is the LORD of hosts," and because Hebrew has no superlative form, the threefold repetition signals the very highest degree, holiness beyond words. It is called communicable because God shares it in measure with His image-bearers; He commands, "Be holy, for I am holy." We will never be holy in the infinite way God is, but by His grace we are called and enabled to reflect His purity in how we live. Love, mercy, justice, and faithfulness are communicable in the same way.

sa.prompt: What does the Shema (Deuteronomy 6:4) declare, and why does it matter for the doctrine of God?
sa.model: The Shema is Israel's foundational confession: "Hear, O Israel: The LORD our God, the LORD is one" (Deuteronomy 6:4). It declares that there is one God, not three gods, and not one God wearing three masks. This matters for the doctrine of God because it guards the truth of biblical monotheism and rules out the idea that the persons of the Trinity are separate deities. When we later confess Father, Son, and Holy Spirit, we never abandon the Shema; we hold the oneness of God and the three persons together. The unity declared here is the fixed point that the doctrine of the Trinity must honor, not contradict.

sa.prompt: Define the Trinity, and explain the difference between a contradiction and a mystery.
sa.model: The Trinity is one God in three persons: the Father, the Son, and the Holy Spirit, one in essence and distinct in person. The Father is not the Son, the Son is not the Spirit, and the Spirit is not the Father, yet each is fully God, not one-third of God. This is not a contradiction but a mystery, and the difference is important. A contradiction violates logic, claiming that one equals three in the same sense at the same time. A mystery exceeds logic, affirming something true that we cannot fully measure or master. The Trinity is one in essence and three in person, distinct categories, so it surpasses our understanding without breaking it.

sa.prompt: How does Acts 2:23 hold together divine sovereignty and human responsibility at the cross?
sa.model: Acts 2:23 says in a single sentence that Jesus was delivered up "by the determined purpose and foreknowledge of God" and that "lawless hands" crucified Him. In other words, God ordained the cross, and men freely committed the cross, and both statements are fully true at once. Divine sovereignty means the cross was no accident; it was God's eternal plan. Human responsibility means the men who carried it out were genuinely guilty of what they did. Neither truth cancels the other. The verse refuses to soften either side, teaching us that God's comprehensive rule and real human accountability stand together, even in the darkest moment of history.

sa.prompt: Why is the doctrine of God's immutability a comfort to believers?
sa.model: Immutability is a comfort because it means the God we trust never changes in character or in His promises. Malachi 3:6 says, "I am the LORD, I do not change," and the unit points out that the same God who comforted Hannah long ago is the same God who comforts a believer tonight, not different by an inch. Our circumstances shift, our moods rise and fall, and people fail us, but God is utterly steady. That means a promise He made does not weaken with time, and His love does not cool when we struggle. Across the longest pause in your prayer life, He is still keeping His word, because His faithfulness flows from a nature that cannot change.

sa.prompt: List and briefly explain three appropriate responses to the doctrine of God.
sa.model: If God is who Scripture says He is, three responses follow. The first is worship: we were made for it, and anything less than this God will eventually disappoint us, so reverence, awe, and obedience are the fitting response to the God who simply is. The second is trust: attributes like aseity, sovereignty, faithfulness, and omniscience are not cold terms but the very reason a believer can sleep at night, because the God who runs the galaxies is attending to the smallest details of our lives. The third is proclamation: our task is not to invent God for people but to introduce them to the God who is already there, reporting an existing reality rather than selling a product.
